title: Gauss-Wilson Theorem: Product of Units and Cyclic Groups
description: Formalizes the Gauss-Wilson theorem: ∏(ℤ/nℤ)* = -1 iff (ℤ/nℤ)* is cyclic, proved via involution lemma and self-inverse classification. Full proof that cyclic → product = -1 and non-cyclic → product = 1. Verifies Gauss-Wilson for all n ≤ 300 and confirms no Wilson primes between 14 and 100. 20 theorems, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Gauss-Wilson theorem generalizes Wilson's theorem: for which n is the product of all units mod n equal to -1? Gauss (1801) proved the answer is exactly n ∈ {1, 2, 4, p^k, 2p^k} — the n with cyclic unit groups. The key algebraic insight is that ∏G = ∏{x | x²=1} for any finite abelian group (elements pair with their inverses, only self-inverse elements contribute).
overview.problemStatement: For which n is ∏(ℤ/nℤ)* = -1 (mod n)? Prove it equals -1 iff (ℤ/nℤ)* is cyclic, using the involution pairing lemma.
overview.text: The key proof is the involution lemma: in any finite abelian group G, pair each element with its inverse. Elements not equal to their inverse cancel in pairs. The remaining product is ∏{x | x²=1}. In a cyclic group with n≥3, the only self-inverse elements are 1 and -1, so ∏{x | x²=1} = -1. In a non-cyclic unit group, there exists a Klein-four subgroup, and the product of a Klein-four group is 1, making the total product 1. This gives the complete characterization.
overview.proofStrategy: Prove the involution lemma: ∏G = ∏{x : x²=1}. Prove cyclic unit groups have exactly {1,-1} as self-inverse elements. Prove non-cyclic groups have ∏ = 1 via Klein-four. Combine for the iff. Bridge to concrete product mod n.
keyInsights: Involution lemma: elements cancel in inverse pairs; only self-inverse elements survive
Cyclic groups: {x | x²=1} = {1,-1} exactly (proved via cyclic generator)
Klein-four subgroup: non-cyclic abelian groups contain ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 → product = 1
The proof is group-theoretic: independent of the specific ring structure of ℤ/nℤ
prerequisites: Finite abelian groups: pairing elements with inverses
Cyclic groups: structure theorem, (ℤ/nℤ)* cyclic iff n ∈ {1,2,4,p^k,2p^k}
Klein-four group: ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 and its product

conclusion.summary: Gauss-Wilson theorem proved: ∏(ℤ/nℤ)* = -1 ↔ (ℤ/nℤ)* cyclic, via involution pairing lemma and Klein-four argument. Verified computationally for n ≤ 300. 20 theorems, 8 definitions, 462 lines, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The Gauss-Wilson theorem characterizes exactly which moduli have a 'Wilson-like' property. It is the algebraic foundation for the structure of unit groups in number theory.
